links.outcome: External discrimination and calibration of PRAISE on local ACS PCI cohort versus reference outcomes
links.effect: C-statistics for death, MI, and major bleeding were 0.75, 0.61, and 0.62; observed to expected ratios 0.427, 0.260, and 0.106, showing poor calibration and limited discrimination locally.
links.quote: The PRAISE score showed limited potential for risk prediction in our validation cohort with acute coronary syndrome.

links.outcome: PRAISE compared with GRACE 2.0, PRECISE-DAPT, and PARIS on discrimination, calibration, reclassification, net benefit
links.effect: PRAISE displayed slightly greater net benefit than GRACE for 1-year death risk at 5%-10% threshold; overall performance limited.
links.quote: Based on the decision curve analysis, the PRAISE score displayed a slightly greater net benefit for the 1-year risk of death (5%-10%) than the GRACE score did.

screen.reason: External validation of an existing machine-learning clinical risk score (PRAISE) in a prospective cohort of Asian ACS patients.
